newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stocks rise in selective speculative trade.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stocks rise in selective speculative trade.

text.p: Jordanian shares crept higher at the start of the week on Saturday on speculative post-holiday buying, dealers said.
The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index rose 0.08 points to 153.28 points in turnover of 836,590 dinars.
A bloc trade worth 292,693 dinars on Jordan Hotel Tourism fixed at an unchanged 8.25 dinars per share accounted for nearly a third of Saturday's turnover.

Brokers said the renewed buying impetus, mainly for non-blue chip shares, by floor traders and institutions, was encouraged by investor expectations of a market rebound when the Moslem Eid al Fitr holiday ends in mid-February.
"The market generally was better on Saturday than Wednesday with movement on more than one of the popular stocks...some investors are buying on hopes of a better market after Eid," one broker said.
The market will close next Saturday for a whole week for the Moslem Eid al-Fitr feast, a public holiday.

Market sentiment has recently improved on signs of institutional buying accompanied by selective foreign purchases that have kept the bourse afloat in the traditionally quiet Moslem fasting month of Ramadan.

The two top gainers, Livestock and Poultry and Jordan International Traders, both rose 3.3 percent to 0.62 dinars. Another strong performer was Industrial, Commercial and Agricultural Company which rose 2.77 percent to 2.60 dinars.
Bluechip heavyweight Arab Bank rose 1.50 dinars to 257 dinars in trade worth 87,305 dinars. Arab Potash Company was unchanged at 5.80 dinars despite 47,208 dinars worth of trade.
Rising shares outnumbered losers by 19 to 13, with 12 unchanged.
The private Pearl Investable Index of the 45 best performing shares on the exchange fell 0.04 percent to 81.43 points.
